f1_driver (08-13): the sensory-anchor motif (a five-point racing harness, re-triggered at every level-up) was drawn directly INTO the cockpitClose backdrop as a chest strap + lap belt + buckle, rather than left audio-only like every prior anchor in this family ([[worn-swords-hip-prop]] samurai's daishō, [[dog-tags-anchor-visual-plant]] special_forces' tags, [[want-object-visual-plant]] mob_boss's Cadillac -- all flagged as needing a reusable worn-prop stage.tsx primitive that was never built). FIRST DRAFT PLACED THE HARNESS WRONG: a plain horizontal rect at y=880-920 for a figure anchored at x=960/y=940/scale=1.4 landed at HAND/HIP height instead of chest height, reading as a bench the figure stood behind rather than a strap across the torso -- caught only by a hand-rendered mid-scene still (frame 309, per [[smoke-covers-only-endpoints]]; the auto frame-0/last-frame smoke would have shown the SAME wrong scene at both checked frames and missed it, since cockpitClose is used at t01/t18/t27/t32 including both endpoints). Fixed by moving the strap geometry up ~110-130px to converge at a buckle roughly at the figure's belt line rather than hand line, and replacing the single rect with two diagonal shoulder-strap paths meeting the lap belt at a central buckle (anatomically closer to a real harness). LESSON for future one-off worn-anchor art: when a backdrop encodes a prop meant to align with a specific figure's body part, the backdrop author needs the figure's actual x/y/scale from the pack wrapper in hand while drawing it, and MUST verify with a mid-scene still at that exact template+frame combination before trusting the geometry -- eyeballing proportions from a different topic's figure (e.g. basketball's iceBathRoom) is not a reliable substitute. Still doesn't produce the reusable stage.tsx primitive those three prior entries called for; this was a bespoke, topic-specific fix.

fbi_undercover (08-02): ThumbPoster in src/thumbs.tsx (line ~564) hardcodes the hero's expression to expr={face('shock')} unconditionally and ignores meta.thumb.expr entirely -- the code comment even notes this was a deliberate reviewer-driven change ('plain FACES.shock read as only a mild o-mouth surprise'), but the practical effect is that thumb.expr is dead data for the poster archetype: whatever a writer sets there (hollow/worried/hardened/etc, per the BIBLE's documented options) never reaches the render. Reusable for any rank ladder where the escalation itself is inexorable and the drama is entirely in what it costs the people around the climber, not the climber's own balance (e.g. a dictator, a cult leader, a cartel plaza boss climbing while lieutenants die around him).

lottery_winner (07-30) traced the root cause behind the recurring 'figure buried behind the caption card' defect family ([[centered-landmark-figure-collision]] etc. are a different failure; this is the CAPTION_SAFE_ZONE note's actual mechanism): director.tsx's CountUp card is `display: inline-block`, auto-sized to whichever is WIDER, the big number (fs84 for any settled label >12 chars, e.g. any 9-figure dollar amount, else fs128) or the gold `sub` line (fs27, letterSpacing 5, roughly ~20-22px/char). The documented '~700px wide' card size in AUTOPILOT_PROMPT is only true for SHORT subs -- a verbose sub-caption (this episode's early drafts ran 50-58 chars) widens the card past 1250-1350px, burying figures that were already positioned at or past CAPTION_SAFE_X=760 by the writer. Confirmed via mid-scene stills: `boardroomNotes` (fig x=960) had its signing figure's torso fully hidden behind a 56-char sub; `fileWall` (fig x=420, scenes.tsx S02) was PARTICULARLY bad -- even with a SHORT sub, the big dollar number alone (~700-780px wide at fs84) already covers fileWall's entire figure, meaning fileWall is structurally incompatible with any dollar overlay at its default figure position, which is likely why prior episodes only ever paired fileWall with overlay=None. FIXED THIS RUN (writer-scope workaround, not a real fix): shortened all subs to ~20-30 chars, moved the new `trailerPorch` figure from x=900 to x=1220, and swapped both `fileWall` overlay-scenes to `deskSilhouette` (fig x=1180, confirmed safe) / `window` (fig x=960 but y=770, high enough to clear). CHEAP REAL FIX for a future engineering pass: cap CountUp's max-width and wrap/shrink the sub-caption font instead of letting the card grow unbounded, OR expose a per-scene safe-figure-x table keyed by template so writers/gate.py can check overlay length against it before render. Until then: writers should keep overlay `sub` under ~30 chars and avoid `fileWall`/`deskClose` (S05, fig x=400) for any scene carrying a big-number overlay.

lottery_winner (07-30) re-hit the exact failure [[template-must-be-registry-key-not-backdrop]] already documents: content.py used `template="suburbHouse"` (that's the REALESTATE pack's BACKDROP name; the actual template key is `openHouse`), and gate.py correctly HALTed after voice+music already ran (~2 min lost, not the ~minutes-long cost noted for could_you_survive_ocean's case since voice cache made the rerun cheap). self_made_billionaire (07-27) first render of the new WASTE pack's `graveside` template placed the cemetery backdrop's fresh-mound-and-flowers ellipse directly behind two standing extras at the same y-band as their legs/waist -- purely a backdrop-vs-standing-figure z-plane coincidence (backdrop always draws behind ALL figures, so 'behind' doesn't mean 'spatially clear'), but it read as the two mourners CARRYING the mound like a stretcher, an unintended and slightly grim misread caught by a manual mid-scene still before it shipped. Fixed by moving the mound off to the side (away from any standing figure's x-range) rather than trying to fix it with z-order (z-order can't separate two things at the same screen height). Same failure family as [[centered-landmark-figure-collision]] (heirGates fountain) but the general form is broader: ANY backdrop element sized/positioned to sit at torso-to-leg height (roughly y740-950 in this stage's coordinate system) needs its x kept clear of wherever standing figures are placed, not just centered landmarks. Cheap checklist item for future new-pack authors: after placing a figure, check every mid-ground backdrop shape at that same y-band for x-overlap before trusting the composition.

self_made_billionaire (07-27): the `routeAftermath` reversal template first shipped with `bg="url(#swarm)"` (warm amber) on the reused SPY `nightStreet` backdrop, and the render read as a warm/cozy evening rather than the grim night-of-the-accident mood the scene needed -- swarm's amber gradient dominated the open sky/ground area even though nightStreet's own internal window-lighting details still drew correctly. Switched to `bg="url(#spaper)"` (the same gradient SPY's own `surveillance` template uses on this backdrop) and it read cooler/moodier immediately. LESSON: when reusing an existing backdrop for a DIFFERENT tonal purpose than its original template, don't assume any bg gradient works just because the backdrop itself has 'night' details baked in -- check what bg the ORIGINAL template paired it with first, since the bg gradient (not just the backdrop shapes) carries most of a scene's mood at the wide shot.

samurai (07-13) exposed a gap between the AUTOPILOT_PROMPT/BIBLE model and duck_music's actual behavior. The prompt tells the writer: 'on the scene IMMEDIATELY BEFORE the reversal line, set gap=1.4' so the music+SFX silence lands before the reversal. But duck_music.py picks the silence-beat location itself — 'the scene whose VO starts nearest 50% of the runtime' (line 75) — and IGNORES the writer's gap= for LOCATION (gap only sizes the fade if it happens to coincide). On samurai the story reversal is the beheading of the mentor at t14 (337s, 44% of a 761s runtime), but because the LATER scenes are longer (dialogue lines + gap=0.7 holds at t24/t26 push the TIME-midpoint past the STORY-midpoint), duck picked t15 (369s, the rival's taunt right after) as nearest-50%, so the silence landed one scene AFTER the intended reversal (still dramatic — it leads into Kenji's 'you put a blade to your own teacher' taunt — but not where the writer aimed it, and the writer's gap=1.4 on t13 did nothing for the silence). This mismatch will recur on ANY episode whose second half is heavier (dialogue/gaps) than its first, which is most of them (the payoff beats cluster late). CHEAP FIX: let a scene dict carry an explicit silence flag (e.g. gap>=1.4 OR a `silence=True` field) that OVERRIDES duck's 50%-nearest auto-pick, so the writer's marked pre-reversal scene is authoritative; fall back to the 50%-nearest heuristic only when no scene is flagged. Pairs with the dramatic-gap system already in gen_voice_edge (gap=0.7/1.4). RECURRED AGAIN on startup_unicorn (07-20): writer set gap=1.4 on t18 (the scene immediately before the t19 down-round reversal line, 50% mark by SCENE INDEX), but duck_music's log shows 'silence beat 0.44s in the gap before t16' instead — two scenes early, landing on the emptyChair/VC-pressure beat rather than the liquidation-preference reversal it was aimed at. Now 3-for-3 confirmed episodes (samurai, startup_unicorn, [ocean was template-error not this]) where the writer's explicit gap=1.4 placement is silently ignored by the 50%-nearest heuristic. Bumping impact med->high: this is a systematic, not occasional, mismatch and the fix is cheap (an explicit override flag, already scoped above). RECURRED A 4TH TIME on zombie_apocalypse (07-21): writer set gap=1.4 on t17 (the quiet 'Mara stops eating' scene, IMMEDIATELY before the t18 bite-reveal reversal line), but duck_music's log again reports 'silence beat 0.45s in the gap before t16' — one scene early, landing in the gap before the barracksLife/exhaustion beat instead of before the reversal. 4-for-4 now; still not fixed because the fix requires editing duck_music.py, which is outside the writer's allowed touch-set (content.py/episode_meta.json/scenes.tsx) for a routine content run — this needs a dedicated engineering pass, not another content-run workaround. COUNTER-EXAMPLE on venture_capitalist (07-24): the writer's gap=1.4 on t16 (the quiet 'phone doesn't buzz' scene, immediately before the t17 fraud-reveal reversal) landed CORRECTLY this time — duck_music.py's own log read 'silence beat 1.30s in the gap before t17', exactly where intended. First correct placement in 5 tracked episodes. Plausible reason, worth testing as a hypothesis rather than treating as confirmed: this script had only ONE other dramatic gap (gap=0.7 at the cold open t01, plus the mirrored gap=0.7 at the very last scene t33) and no dialogue-heavy back half, so nothing in the SECOND half of the runtime was heavier/longer than the first half — unlike the 4 prior mismatched episodes, which all had extra gap=0.7/1.4 holds or dialogue clustering AFTER their intended silence point, pulling the runtime-nearest-50% heuristic later than the scene-index midpoint. If this holds up across more episodes, the cheap mitigation until duck_music.py gets the real override-flag fix: keep dramatic gap=0.7/1.4 holds and dialogue scenes roughly BALANCED between the two halves of the script, not concentrated in the second half, so the writer's intended silence-beat scene stays close to the runtime midpoint the heuristic actually picks. SECOND correct placement on yakuza (07-31): writer set gap=1.4 on t15 (scene 15/30, 50% by scene-index, immediately before the t16 split/hamon/Sato's-death reversal), and duck_music's log read 'silence beat 1.30s in the gap before t16' — exactly where intended. This script kept its 3 dramatic gaps spread across the runtime (gap=0.7 at t01 cold open, gap=1.4 at t15, gap=0.7 at t26 kumicho ascension) rather than clustered late, and dialogue lines (t05/t08/t16/t29) were similarly spread across both halves rather than back-loaded — consistent with the venture_capitalist hypothesis above. 2-for-2 now when gaps/dialogue stay balanced across the runtime; still 4-for-4 mismatched when they cluster in the second half. Strengthens the case for the balanced-placement mitigation as a real, repeatable content-run workaround pending the actual override-flag fix in duck_music.py. THIRD correct placement on ottoman_empire (08-06): writer set gap=1.4 on t16 (scene 16/32, immediately before the t17 cauldronRevolt/1622-regicide reversal), and duck_music's log read 'silence beat 1.30s in the gap before t17' — exactly where intended. Gaps again spread across the runtime (gap=0.7 at t01 cold open, gap=1.4 at t16, gap=0.7 at t29 Grand Vizier ascension) and the 3 dialogue lines (t07 mentor warning, t17 rival taunt, t31 pre-loop-close) landed at the exact BIBLE-prescribed spots rather than clustering late. 3-for-3 now when gaps/dialogue stay balanced across the runtime — the balanced-placement mitigation looks like a reliable, repeatable content-run workaround at this point, not just a hypothesis.

could_you_survive_ocean (07-10) was resumed from an INTERRUPTED run whose content.py referenced TWO scene backdrops as if they were templates: t01 template='seaDeck' (seaDeck is a DYNASTY *backdrop*; the template that renders it is yachtDeck) and t13 template='stormSea' (stormSea is a *backdrop* used by oceanCapsize, not a template). The gate correctly HALTed ('template X not in registry') but only AFTER voice+music+bundle ran (~minutes). This is a recurring interrupted-run hazard because a backdrop and a template often share a concept name (seaDeck/yachtDeck, stormSea/oceanCapsize). Fixes shipped this run: added two proper OCEAN templates — boatDeck (working-sailor comfort beat on the seaDeck backdrop, distinct from DYNASTY yachtDeck's smug heir) and rainSquall (the squall/rain-catch mercy beat on the stormSea backdrop). CHEAP GUARD IDEA: build.py already imports content + can import PACK_TEMPLATES keys via a tiny node/grep — assert every scene['template'] is a PACK_TEMPLATES key BEFORE the expensive voice step (move the registry check that gate.py already does to the top, next to the syntax gate), so a bad template name fails in seconds, not minutes. Pairs with [[meta-topic-mismatch-guard]] (both catch interrupted/partial-run state cheaply).

could_you_survive_ocean (07-10): the SCALETERROR archetype (thumbs.tsx ThumbScaleTerror) renders the KICKER+L1 caption as a Punch at (70,150) fs48 and the red KeyPill at (78, 150+kw) where kw~=88 for a 9-char keyword — the pill's rotated box top reaches up into the caption's baseline, so 'NO RESCUE' sat ON TOP of '1,200 MILES FROM LAND' and hid all but the trailing 'AND' (looked broken). Also for an OCEAN topic the giant INK humanoid 'threat' shape reads as a looming PERSON, not the sea — a confusing metaphor for a water-survival video. Rendering the thumbnail post-build (the [[package-before-review]] habit) caught both before review; switched to the eyeline archetype (big worried face + arrow + withheld '?' + NO RESCUE) which rendered clean and on-emotion. CHEAP FIXES for scaleterror: (a) push the KICKER+L1 caption ABOVE the pill (y small, e.g. y=60) or move the pill down so its box never overlaps the caption; (b) for scale-terror on NON-humanoid threats (ocean, avalanche, fire) let a meta field pick the looming shape (wave/wall vs figure). Pairs with [[number-thumb-collision-short-values]] + [[beforeafter-hero-expr-hardcoded]] — same family of thumbnail layout gaps.

trillionaire (07-07) validated the SCENARIO format (first non-rank/non-history/non-survival episode) AND a fourth spine flavor: a PURE MONEY ladder where the on-screen gold number CLIMBS ($0 -> $1M -> $100M -> $1B -> $100B -> $1T) while the SUB-caption tracks what you can actually SPEND FALLING to nothing ('NOT CASH · A PROMISE ON PAPER' -> 'YOU NEVER SELL' -> 'YOU CAN'T SELL IT · CASH OUT AND THE NUMBER DIES'). The drama is the GAP between the exploding paper number and the collapsing spendable amount — the apex twist is that a trillionaire owns, spendably, $0. Distinct from [[valuation-vs-personal-spine]] (built vs kept), [[inverted-spine-validated]] (power vs frozen pay), [[control-vs-own-spine-validated]] (control vs own): here it's PAPER vs SPENDABLE. Composed entirely from STARTUP (garageStart/startupGrow/serverScale/ipoBell) + FINANCE (tradingFloor/pnlWall) + DYNASTY (galaBallroom/yachtDeck/familyVault) + generic (podiumScene) + universal — NO bespoke TSX, 28 scenes, 13.0 min, gate PASS 0 warnings. Reusable for lottery_winner, and any scenario where escalating MILLIONS/DECISIONS are the level labels. The two share-beats (trillion seconds = ~31,700 yrs; $1M/day since Christ ~= $740B, still not $1T) are arithmetically verified and landed as the 'wait, that's real?' plants (research doc trillionaire.md).

trillionaire used a SOUND/EMOTIONAL anchor — Dani's 19-SECOND VOICEMAIL (her laugh, 'eat something, call me back'): saved t02, replayed t16, she calls LIVE at the trillion and you let it ring t18 (cold-open payoff), replayed one last time at loop-close t25. Because the anchor is inherently a SOUND, not a worn/carried object, it sidesteps the recurring 'audio-only anchor never drawn on the figure' defect family ([[worn-swords-hip-prop]], [[dog-tags-anchor-visual-plant]], [[want-object-visual-plant]]) — there is nothing to draw, so nothing is missing visually; the '19 SECONDS' overlay at t25 carries the payoff on-screen. LESSON: when a topic has no natural WORN object, a recurring sound/recording/number anchor tied to a named person is a clean choice that avoids the undrawn-prop trap entirely and still gives the overlay a concrete callback ('19 SECONDS'). Secondary sensory texture (burnt $4.50 gas-station coffee) rode alongside as the 'money never upgrades this about you' motif.

special_forces (07-04) shipped with NO new template pack — it composed the whole 8-level ladder (candidate/selection -> operator/ODA -> team sergeant -> the tier-1 Unit -> assault commander -> squadron -> joint task force -> the man who signs) entirely from the existing MILITARY pack (bootcamp=selection ruck+the loop, barracksLife=empty bunks/drawer of tags, frontline=the breach/combat/raid, commandPost=team & troop command, decoration=the tab/no-medal) + the SPY pack (tradecraft=selection ground/kill house, surveillance=night infil, safehouse=the HVT target wall, debrief=the tasking/mentor warning, station=the joint command) + universal (warRoom=JSOC apex, emptyChair=the rival's empty chair, signing=the order, jet=deployment). No adjacent repeats across 30 scenes. Confirms the SPY+MILITARY packs cover the whole special-operations / covert-military space — reusable for fbi_undercover, secret_service, PMC/mercenary, hostage-rescue topics with zero bespoke TSX. Pairs with [[spy-pack-validated]] + [[more-domain-packs]].

special_forces made 'dog tags, TAPED so they don't rattle' (sound discipline) the sensory anchor — loud at selection (t01), taped before the first infil (t05), checked on the team (t07), NONE/sterile at the Unit (t10), a dead man's tags carried out at the midpoint (t14), a drawer of them (t17), a new candidate's rattling at the loop-close (t28). Strong callback engine, but like samurai's daishō [[worn-swords-hip-prop]] and the mob Cadillac [[want-object-visual-plant]] it is AUDIO-ONLY — the taped tags are never drawn on the POV figure, so the 'sterile/empty' and 'drawer of the dead' payoffs don't read visually. Same fix family: a tiny 'tags at the chest' figure primitive that MILITARY/SPY templates toggle ON (loose) at L1, TAPED from L2, OFF (sterile) at L4, so the anchor the narration keeps tightening tightens on screen. Generalizes to any small worn/carried anchor object (ring, badge, tags, coin).

samurai (07-04) made THE WEIGHT OF THE TWO SWORDS AT THE LEFT HIP the sensory anchor motif — it 'arrives' at t04 (daisho), is re-triggered at every level-up ('the swords are heavier today'), and is stripped bare at t25 (Haitōrei ban, 'your hip goes light'). But the daishō is only DRAWN once, on the sword stand at t04; the POV figure never visibly WEARS the swords across the climb, and the t25 payoff ('hip goes bare') is audio-only. Same failure family as [[want-object-visual-plant]] (mob_boss's undrawn Cadillac). Fix: a small 'sheathed daishō at the left hip' figure primitive in stage.tsx (a short + long line at the belt) that the SAMURAI templates toggle ON from L2 and OFF at the ban scene — so the anchor the narration keeps tightening is actually visible tightening, and the empty hip at the end reads at a glance. Generalizes to any worn want-object anchor (a ring, a badge, a holster).

mob_boss (07-01) got a 'revise' verdict whose ONLY blocker was pipeline order: daily_autopilot renders out/thumbnail.png + gen_packaging.py (upload_kit.json) at step 5 AFTER the review loop, so the reviewer sees the PREVIOUS episode's stale files on disk and correctly refuses to approve (a Roman 'YOU ARE MORTAL' thumb would have shipped on the Mafia video if not caught). Cheap fix: move `npx remotion still Thumbnail` + `python3 gen_packaging.py` to right after build (or into build.py step order) so the on-disk packaging always matches the episode under review; publish step can re-run them idempotently. Costs one 5s still per build; saves a whole render->review->fix cycle. MITIGATED MANUALLY on billionaire_heir (07-03) AND mexican_cartel (07-06): showrunner rendered the Thumbnail still (out/thumbnail.png) + ran gen_packaging.py (out/upload_kit.json) right after BUILD OK, so on-disk packaging matches the episode under review. On mexican_cartel this also CAUGHT the number-thumb collision [[number-thumb-collision-short-values]] before review — rendering the thumb post-build is doubling as a thumbnail QA gate, another reason to make it a permanent pipeline step. The pipeline-order fix in daily_autopilot/build.py is still the real cure.

docs/research/mob_boss.md ended with stray literal '</content>\n</invoke>' lines — a prior agent's tool-call syntax leaked into the written file. Harmless here (research doc), but if it happened inside content.py or episode_meta.json the syntax gate would HALT a build. Idea: build.py (or gate.py) grep the creative-owned text files for tool-call markers (</invoke>, </content>, <function_results) and warn, so a corrupted write is caught at build time, not at review.

surgeon proved the escalation spine works for a NON-money ladder where the bottom is DEBT and the apex is a SYSTEM ($5.3T), not a personal salary. Reusable pattern for soldier/doctor/politician: open on the system's total scale, end on 'they decide what X is worth.' Medical pack + lectureHall/podium covered every beat with no bespoke scenes.

founder ep used COMPANY VALUATION as the on-screen big-number spine ($0->$6M->...->$1B->$6B->$209B) with the founder's lagging personal money (salary, paper stake, % owned) in the SUB-caption. Sharpens the gap between what you BUILT and what you KEEP — reusable for any equity/ownership ladder (real_estate_mogul, hedge_fund, software_engineer FAANG->founder->VC). The dilution beat '100% -> 36%' as a non-dollar ratio overlay landed well.

founder ep introduced non-dollar overlays for dramatic beats: a dilution ratio ('100% -> 36%') and a stat-as-power line ('9 IN 10 FAIL'). These read fine in the gold number style but a distinct visual treatment (e.g. arrow/percentage glyph, or the red/amber from negative-number-color) would let ratios/odds register as a different KIND of number than the $ spine. Pairs with the still-open negative-number-color item.

soldier ep proved an INVERTED spine: the on-screen big number is NON-MONEY power (TROOPS UNDER YOUR COMMAND: 0 -> 9 -> 150 -> 700 -> 4,500 -> 20,000 -> 200,000) while PERSONAL PAY stays small, flat, and CAPS in the sub-caption (~$25K -> ~$221K). The drama is the GAP between exploding power and frozen pay — the opposite of the finance ladders where money is the spine. Apex flips to the system that POINTS the force ($895B budget / $2.7T global spend) and the civilians who never bleed. Reusable for politician (constituents/votes commanded vs a fixed salary), and any rank/authority ladder where power, not pay, is the escalation. RE-VALIDATED by spy: REACH (ASSETS 0 -> 4 -> ~20 -> ONE STATION -> A REGION -> EVERY COVERT OP -> 21,000 OFFICERS -> THE PEOPLE ABOVE) explodes in the overlay while GS pay stays capped in the sub ($66K -> ~$200K, 'you never get rich'); the only $ count-up is the apex $106B secret budget at cold-open + close. Pairs with [[non-finance-spine-validated]].

NOW 6th+ episode with a COST/loss overlay rendered in the SAME gold as income: surgeon -$235K debt, hedge -$22M drawdown, soldier -1 KIA, real_estate 'FIRST EVICTION' + '100 UNITS CLEARED', spy 'BURNED', and roman_empire 'THE FARM IS SOLD' + 'ONE IN TEN' (decimation) + 'MURDERED'. The pattern is now load-bearing on the moral-erosion beats of EVERY topic. Bumped to HIGH: a red/amber treatment for negative/cost overlays (and a distinct glyph for ratio/stat overlays per [[ratio-overlay-treatment]]) vs gold for gain is the single highest-value visual upgrade left. Pairs with the still-open [[negative-number-color]].

real_estate_mogul ep validated a LEVERAGE spine: the on-screen big number is ASSETS YOU CONTROL ($0 -> 300K -> 4M -> 40M -> 250M -> 2B -> 600B -> $393T) driven by debt + other people's money, while the personal cut / down payment / equity lags in the gold SUB-caption ('~$60K DOWN', 'NONE OF IT YOURS'). It's the third spine flavor after [[valuation-vs-personal-spine]] (what you BUILT vs KEEP) and [[inverted-spine-validated]] (power vs frozen pay): here it's what you CONTROL vs what you OWN. Reusable for any leverage/OPM ladder (private equity, leveraged trading, franchising). Apex flips to the asset class itself + the capital that prices it.

spy reviewer (approve, score 8) flagged that the 'station' template at LEVEL 04 (chief of station, t11) is visually near-identical to LEVEL 02 (case officer, t04) — both correct & non-adjacent, so no BIBLE rule broken, but the jump in REACH reads only from the overlay text, not the staging. When the same topic-appropriate template is the right fit at two different LEVELS, the director engine could scale the staging by level depth (wider frame / more background figures / bigger desk count at the higher rung) so a reused template still reads as escalation, not repetition. Generalizes beyond spy (any ladder where one setting is the natural home for two ranks: tradingFloor analyst->PM, operatingRoom resident->attending). Cheap win in src/stage.tsx or director.tsx; pairs with the multi-shot director. RECONFIRMED by mob_boss (07-01): reviewer flagged the 'two figures at a bar' look recurring ~6x across redSauce+socialClub (associate rules -> made-man earn -> capo sit-down -> Sal's murder -> the rat) with no visual escalation between ranks; one swap (t18->backAlley) reduced it but the by-level staging scaler remains the real fix.

build.py smoke render only checks frame 0 (which is the fade-in -> BLANK) + the last frame, so a bespoke prop/backdrop used only mid-scene is NEVER smoke-tested and a render-time error or an ugly composition (the roman 'chariot' first read as ambiguous blobs) ships unseen. For roman I had to hand-render ~12 mid-scene stills to catch it. Cheap fix: when content.py introduces NEW template keys not in the previous episode, build.py should auto-render one mid-scene still per new template (pick frame = scene.startFrame + dur/2 from timeline.json) into out/_smoke_packs/ and HALT/warn on render error. Closes the QA gap between the 1-frame smoke and the post-render reviewer. CONFIRMED AGAIN on pirate (08-08): manually rendered 7 mid-scene stills (one per new PIRATE-pack template) before shipping and it caught THREE real defects a frame-0/last-frame smoke would have missed entirely -- broadsideBattle's deck cannon sat exactly behind the money-card safe zone (see the new caption-safe-zone-on-backdrop-prop entry below), nassauHarbor's palm-tree fronds were staged mid-trunk instead of as a top canopy (read as stray sticks, not palms), and the same template's background 'anchored ships' were bare vertical lines with no hull (read as a forest of masts, not boats). All three fixed same session after a visual spot-check, none would have failed gate.py or the syntax/frame-0/last-frame smoke. Fourth confirmed case (after roman's chariot, spy's restage flag, and black_market_surgeon's relit-backdrop checks) that new bespoke art needs an eyeball pass, not just the automated gate.

The roman chariot (quadriga: gold car + spoked wheel + a 2-horse profile team) was bespoke and took a restage to read clearly. A small reusable library of side-profile ANIMAL/VEHICLE primitives (horse, cart, mounted rider, boat) in stage.tsx would speed up upcoming queue topics that need them: samurai (mounted), gladiator (chariot), pirate (ship/deck), king (horse/cavalry), astronaut (capsule). Keep the clean doodle profile shape from roman's chariot horses as the template.

roman_empire validated a DUAL spine that combines the money ladder and the reach ladder in ONE overlay: gold $ census steps (0 DENARII -> 225/yr -> ~450 -> ~3,375 -> 400,000 SESTERCES -> 1,000,000 -> ALL OF ROME) interleaved with non-$ reach/cost beats (ONE IN TEN decimation, THE FARM IS SOLD, 15,000/GUARD donativum, 9,000 GUARDS, MURDERED, 25,000 SESTERCES/MAN auction). The apex twist 'even the throne has a per-man price (the 193 AD auction)' is a strong share beat. Reusable for any historical rank ladder where real coin AND real power both escalate (samurai/daimyo, medieval king, mongol). Pairs with [[non-finance-spine-validated]] and [[negative-overlay-recurring]].

docs/bibles/QUALITY_MAX_PLAN.md. Phases 1-5 SHIPPED 06-28 (Story+Packaging, Audio, Animation, Color, Thumbnails). Remaining: 6 Polish(transitions/boil/static-grain/sectioned score) — the deferred heavier/riskier set.

Follow-up to [[edge-tts-retry-resilience]]. gen_voice_edge.py still re-synthesizes ALL 28 scenes from the network on every build run, even when only content changed for a few (or a prior run already produced 27 good wavs). Two cheap wins: (1) per-scene CACHE keyed by a hash of (narration text + VOICE + RATE) -> skip synth+master when the cached wav matches, so a HALT-and-rerun reuses good scenes and only the failed/edited one re-hits the network (turns a ~2-3min voice step into seconds on reruns); (2) optionally a small bounded asyncio.gather pool (2-3 concurrent) to shorten cold builds. Caution: cache must invalidate on any narration edit (hash the text, not just the scene id) or it ships stale audio. Lives in gen_voice_edge.py.

mob_boss revise: Nicky (the entire Level-8 payoff) was first named at ~85% of runtime. Add a cheap gate check: any proper name appearing in the last third of content.py must also appear in the first two-thirds (plant before payoff). Catches unplanted-payoff bugs at build time instead of review.

mob_boss reviewer: cardGame/socialClub/redSauce/mobTable all read as the same beige bar-counter room (same bottle shelf/pictures/candle), so Sal's murder, the made-man payday and the rat reveal play in what looks like one location and pattern interrupts don't register. billionaire_heir (07-03) run started from an INTERRUPTED prior run: content.py + research + dynasty pack were already written for billionaire_heir, but ops/episode_meta.json still held mob_boss. If build+render had run in that state, the heir video would have shipped with the Mafia title/description/thumbnail. heirGates first render placed the POV figure at x=960 — dead center on the estateGrounds fountain (also centered) — so the basin+jet read as a thought bubble sitting on the figure's head. mob_boss: the black Cadillac (the named want-object opening and closing the loop) was never drawn — the cyclical echo was audio-only. mexican_cartel (07-06): the NUMBER archetype (thumbs.tsx ThumbNumber) collides for SHORT $ values. BIG font = min(480, 1300/len*1.6), so a 3-char value like '$85' maxes at 480px and the giant number sits over the top kicker/line1 caption — 'A HIT PAYS' was almost entirely hidden behind the '$85', only '..YS' peeked out (looked broken). Had to abandon the strongest hook (a life costs $85 = DISPOSABLE) and switch the thumb to beforeafter (NOBODY -> HUNTED). Cheap fix: when BIG.length is small, cap fs lower (e.g. min(360,...)) AND/OR move the kicker+line1 caption OUT of the number's box (top-left small, or below the accent bar) so a short shock-number thumb is usable. The low-horror-number thumb ($85/$30-a-hit) is a high-CTR angle worth unlocking. Pairs with [[negative-overlay-recurring]] (both are thumbnail/overlay number-treatment gaps).

mexican_cartel (07-06): ThumbBefore (beforeafter archetype) hardcodes the AFTER hero's face to expr='smug' (`expr={face('smug')}`) and ignores meta thumb.expr, so a 'HUNTED'/fear pairing renders a calm neutral stare instead of the worried/shock face that is the #1 CTR lever with no real faces. ThumbPov already reads t.expr correctly. One-line fix: make ThumbBefore's Hero use expr={face(t.expr || 'smug')} so the after-figure's emotion can match the after-word (shock/worried for a HUNTED/BURNED/TRAPPED apex). Rendered fine this run (cold narco reads OK), flagged as a cheap CTR upgrade.

mexican_cartel (07-06): cut ~85 words (2725->2643) and runtime only moved 13.8->13.5 min, because per-scene GAP padding (0.25 default + LEAD) plus the deliberate gap=0.7/1.4 dramatic holds dominate a 29-scene episode, not the narration length. LESSON for over-length episodes: the effective runtime levers are (a) drop a whole scene (~27s each) or (b) reduce/relocate a dramatic gap — shaving words gives diminishing returns (~0.2s per word). Note: 13.5 min still shipped (founder 14.1 min is the top performer, roman 13.1 min shipped), so the ~13 ceiling is soft with cloud render; but if a HALT ever needs real trimming, cut scenes, not words. Could add a build.py readout of 'padding vs speech' seconds so the writer sees where the runtime actually goes.

black_market_surgeon (07-15): the new BLACKMARKET pack's syndicateClinic/coldCase templates add a DIM extra figure meant to read as an armed guard/courier, but the extra is the same generic silhouette used everywhere else (no weapon/prop distinguishing it) — at 120px thumbnail scale or a quick glance it just reads as 'another person', not specifically a threat. Cheap fix: a tiny optional prop toggle on the figure primitive (a short diagonal line = a slung rifle silhouette, doodle-consistent) that guard/security extras across ANY pack (spy safehouse, cartel ranchCompound, mafia donOffice) could opt into, so 'this person is armed' reads at a glance instead of only through narration.

self_made_billionaire (07-27), FINAL REVIEWER catch (high severity, decision=revise): the `dawnRoute`/`routeAftermath` templates drew the `wasteTruck` prop with `figBehind` while placing the figure at the SAME default-ish coordinates the truck's opaque compactor-box silhouette covers (prop footprint roughly x470-1370/y716-960 at the truck's fixed translate(925,960); figure at x900,y906 sits dead center inside it). `figBehind` draws the figure FIRST then the prop OVER it, so a large opaque prop whose footprint envelops the figure's x/y doesn't read as 'figure standing behind/inside the vehicle' -- it reads as the figure split in half, only the head above the roofline and legs below the chassis, because the prop's mid-body shapes are fully opaque. This hit t03/t10/t17 AND t18 (the midpoint-reversal death scene, the episode's most important beat). FIX: for a large-footprint prop like a vehicle where the figure should stand beside/in front of it (not literally behind an opening it looks through), don't use figBehind at all -- let the figure draw last (default order) so it composites cleanly in front of the prop. Reserve figBehind for props with a real opening/frame the figure sits inside (life raft, chariot, cell bars) where the prop's shapes DON'T fully cover the figure's silhouette. CHEAP CHECKLIST for future vehicle/large-object props: sketch the prop's local bounding box, translate it to screen coords, and check whether the figure's default x/y falls inside it before deciding figBehind vs default order.

self_made_billionaire (07-27), FINAL REVIEWER catch (low severity): tried to differentiate two identical background-mourner extras (both `A.stand`, `pal: DIM`, `face: false`, front view) by giving the second one `view: 'profile'` plus a `headTilt` override, expecting it to read as a distinct turned/glancing figure per the narration ('a woman in a black coat glances back'). It rendered visually identical to the first -- in src/figure.tsx's StickFigure, `view`/`front` only changes which side ('near' vs 'far') the limb-mirroring uses (`ffar = front ? -facing : facing`); the <Face> component is called with `profile={false}` UNCONDITIONALLY, so the face itself never turns or changes shape based on `view`. LESSON: `view: 'profile'` alone is not a usable tool for visually distinguishing two otherwise-identical background figures in this rig -- it's a subtle limb-offset difference, not a silhouette change. To make a background figure read as distinct (a different person, a turned head, a glance), use `face: true` with a directional `expr` (e.g. FACES.conflicted has look:-0.45, 'uneasy, looking away') instead -- a visible eye/brow/mouth reads as a real differentiator at thumbnail-adjacent crowd scale where a blank oval does not.
